title: The ringed projection mate commutes with shifts in its direct-image input
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,A_X)\to(\mathscr Y,A_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the coefficient universe, with sheaves of commutative rings and a map $f^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$. Use the unbounded derived module-sheaf categories, ordinary K-flat derived tensor, K-injective derived direct image, and canonical derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Write $U=Lf^*$, $R=Rf_*$ and $\varepsilon:UR\to1$. Give $U$ its canonical integer-shift structure and $R$ the unique unit/counit-compatible shift structure of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]. Let $\mu:U(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Y}N)\cong UM\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}UN$ be the canonical pullback tensor comparison. For $K\in D(A_X)$ and $P\in D(A_Y)$ let
$$\pi_{K,P}:RK\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Y}P\longrightarrow R(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}UP)$$
be the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)\circ\mu_{RK,P}$.

For each fixed $P$, the functors $F_P(K)=RK\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Y}P$ and $G_P(K)=R(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}UP)$ are exact, and $\pi_{-,P}$ is a natural transformation commuting with their induced shift isomorphisms. Explicitly, writing $s_F:F_P(K[1])\cong F_P(K)[1]$ and $s_G:G_P(K[1])\cong G_P(K)[1]$, one has
$$s_G\circ\pi_{K[1],P}=\pi_{K,P}[1]\circ s_F.$$
Thus it gives a morphism of distinguished triangles in the $K$ variable, including the connecting square. No invertibility of $\pi_{K,P}$ is asserted.

proof.text: The exact derived pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] is $U$ in the canonical adjunction supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. The hypotheses are precisely the small ringed sites and the coefficient map in the statement; no flatness of that map is needed. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique], the prescribed shift on $R$ is coherent and both unit $\eta:1\to RU$ and counit $\varepsilon:UR\to1$ commute with shifts. Apply [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] to this exact $U$ and this adjunction: $R$ is exact with the prescribed shift.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; derived.tex Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact

proof.text:
Fix $P$ and abbreviate $T_Y(M)=M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Y}P$, $H(K)=T_X(K)=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}UP$. Both tensor functors are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Write $u_M:U(M[1])\to(UM)[1]$, $r_K:R(K[1])\to(RK)[1]$, and $t_Y(M):T_Y(M[1])\to T_Y(M)[1]$, $t_X(K):H(K[1])\to H(K)[1]$ for their natural shift maps. Then $F=T_YR$ and $G=RH$ are exact: applying their two factors successively to any distinguished triangle gives a distinguished triangle. Their induced shift maps, as in [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker], are
$$s_F(K)=t_Y(RK)\circ(r_K\otimes1),\qquad s_G(K)=r_{H(K)}\circ R(t_X(K)).$$
The composite $UF$ has shift map $s_{UF}(K)=u_{F(K)}\circ U(s_F(K))$, and $UR$ has $s_{UR}(K)=u_{RK}\circ U(r_K)$. All are coherent composite structures.

source.place: Tags 06YU, definition-derived-tor, and 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; derived.tex Tag 014Y, lemma-composition-exact

proof.text:
Put $\beta_K=(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)\circ\mu_{RK,P}:UF(K)\to H(K)$. The adjunction formula in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] gives
$$\pi_{K,P}=R(\beta_K)\circ\eta_{F(K)}.$$
The naturality in $K$ asserted by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] applies to exactly this projection mate (its variable $E$ is our $K$, and its variable $P$ is our fixed $P$). Thus $\pi_{-,P}$ is natural, with no assertion that its components are invertible.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, definition by adjoint transpose

proof.text:
By the first-factor shift compatibility and naturality of $\mu$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact],
$$t_X(URK)\circ(s_{UR}(K)\otimes1)\circ\mu_{R(K[1]),P}
 =\mu_{RK,P}[1]\circ s_{UF}(K).$$
Here is the substitution specifying the square. First use naturality at $r_K:R(K[1])\to(RK)[1]$:
$$(U(r_K)\otimes1)\circ\mu_{R(K[1]),P}=\mu_{(RK)[1],P}\circ U(r_K\otimes1).$$
Then use the shift square at $M=RK$:
$$t_X(URK)\circ(u_{RK}\otimes1)\circ\mu_{(RK)[1],P}
 =\mu_{RK,P}[1]\circ u_{T_Y(RK)}\circ U(t_Y(RK)).$$
Composing and substituting the expressions from step 2 gives the displayed equation. This uses the canonical tensor comparison, rather than an arbitrary strong monoidal structure.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; canonical comparison on total K-flat tensor complexes, first-factor shift square

proof.text:
The counit identity of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] is
$$\varepsilon_{K[1]}=\varepsilon_K[1]\circ s_{UR}(K).$$
Tensor it with $1_{UP}$ and use the naturality of $t_X$ at $\varepsilon_K:URK\to K$. Substitution in step 4 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
t_X(K)\circ\beta_{K[1]}
 &=t_X(K)\circ(\varepsilon_K[1]\otimes1)\circ(s_{UR}(K)\otimes1)\circ\mu_{R(K[1]),P}\\
 &=(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)[1]\circ t_X(URK)\circ(s_{UR}(K)\otimes1)\circ\mu_{R(K[1]),P}\\
 &=\beta_K[1]\circ s_{UF}(K).
\end{aligned}$$
The tensor shift maps are natural because they are the shift structures of the exact tensor functors supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact].

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; derived.tex Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact; counit-compatible shift identity

proof.text:
Naturality of $\eta$ at $s_F(K):F(K[1])\to F(K)[1]$ and the unit-compatible shift identity of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] give
$$r_{UF(K)}\circ R(s_{UF}(K))\circ\eta_{F(K[1])}
 =r_{UF(K)}\circ R(u_{F(K)})\circ\eta_{F(K)[1]}\circ s_F(K)
 =\eta_{F(K)}[1]\circ s_F(K).$$
Use step 5 and naturality of $r$ at $\beta_K:UF(K)\to H(K)$ to compute
$$\begin{aligned}
s_G(K)\circ\pi_{K[1],P}
 &=r_{H(K)}\circ R(t_X(K)\circ\beta_{K[1]})\circ\eta_{F(K[1])}\\
 &=r_{H(K)}\circ R(\beta_K[1])\circ R(s_{UF}(K))\circ\eta_{F(K[1])}\\
 &=(R\beta_K)[1]\circ r_{UF(K)}\circ R(s_{UF}(K))\circ\eta_{F(K[1])}\\
 &=(R\beta_K)[1]\circ\eta_{F(K)}[1]\circ s_F(K)
 =\pi_{K,P}[1]\circ s_F(K).
\end{aligned}$$
The first and last equalities use the adjunct formula in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. This is the required shift square.

proof.text:
For a distinguished triangle $K_1\xrightarrow a K_2\xrightarrow b K_3\xrightarrow c K_1[1]$, step 2 gives distinguished image triangles with connecting arrows $s_F(K_1)\circ F(c)$ and $s_G(K_1)\circ G(c)$. The three components $\pi_{K_i,P}$ satisfy the first two squares by naturality. For the connecting square, naturality at $c$ followed by step 6 gives
$$s_G(K_1)\circ G(c)\circ\pi_{K_3,P}
 =s_G(K_1)\circ\pi_{K_1[1],P}\circ F(c)
 =\pi_{K_1,P}[1]\circ s_F(K_1)\circ F(c).$$
These are exactly the three defining equations for a morphism of triangles in [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift].
